newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Coffee due lower, seen trading sideways.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Coffee due lower, seen trading sideways.

text.p: SEPT Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA40
The fall in coffee has lost momentum and the market should trade sideways or move higher, analysts said on Wednesday.
Traders said it was due on numbers to open around $30 down. One trader said an opening fall of $10 to $15 was more likely.
"We should see sideways or higher trading," analyst Susan Rigg of Chart Analysis said. "A close above $2,000 would take it to higher levels."
"Good support should soften the risk on the downside," she said.
However, the market was still a bit shattered after its sharp fall from contract highs, even though the fall had lost momentum," Rigg said.
"It's going to have to do some work before it goes up," she said.
New York coffee futures ended higher on Tuesday, but sharply off peaks, after the latest Brazilian weather forecasts reduced the chances of crop-damaging cold this weekend, traders said.
No damaging cold is indicated for the next seven days in Brazil's coffee regions, independent forecaster Weather Services Corporation said on Wednesday.

Administrative workers at the key Brazilian port of Santos have decided to continue their strike for at least another day and new talks with the port authority will be needed to solve the dispute, a spokesman said.
Brazilian coffee exporters were watching the strike but said the stoppage had come at a quiet time for coffee shipments and would only affect coffee if it continued beyond a couple of days.

"Shipments have fallen substantially in June. If the strike carries on for only two or three days, it will have zero impact," said Jorge Esteve, president of the Brazilian Coffee Exporters' Association, based in Santos.
